about: Settled negatives: dead ends from the Nov 11 2026 mystery-parks pass. Do not search them again. Entries with miss_proves_nothing=true are the reverse: a miss there is no evidence, so look elsewhere. Human note: settled-negatives.md. Read only; nothing here writes a key, an override or a pin.
source: Nov 11 2026 notes (nov11/MYSTERY_PARKS_NOV11_NOTES.md), section 9; layer rows in sources/research-sources-all.csv

negatives.scope: BLM state offices: Idaho, Wyoming, Utah, Nevada, California
negatives.statement: BLM publishes no site-level polygons at state level. Idaho has only SRMAs (the bigger place, never taken); Wyoming has points; Utah has congressional recreation areas only; Nevada has nothing; California has nothing at Laguna Mountain (US-13513, nothing within 8 km). An official BLM point may be recorded as an official point, never as a boundary.
negatives.do_not: search these BLM state layers again for a site polygon

negatives.scope: Nov 11 answers file: the 15 rows answered "no boundary exists"
negatives.statement: All 15 stand. The official source shows a road, a roadside marker, a route or a single monument: there is no land unit to outline. A second look (follow-up pass) added ids and points and kept every answer.
negatives.do_not: search these parks for a boundary again

negatives.scope: Tennessee TDEC Division of Natural Areas layer
negatives.statement: The layer is incomplete (no Ozone Falls, Window Cliffs or Sellars Farm; Pogue Creek Canyon has only a 58-acre piece 6.7 km away). A miss on this layer proves nothing: use PAD-US from USGS, the other official polygon.
negatives.do_not: treat a miss on this layer as "no boundary"

negatives.scope: National Park Service National Register public layer
negatives.statement: The public layer withholds sensitive sites (Spiro Mounds and Fort Towson are absent). A miss there proves nothing for such sites.
negatives.do_not: treat a National Register miss as "no boundary" for a sensitive site
